blocks.content: Regional metamorphism affects extensive areas of the Earth's crust and is primarily driven by large-scale tectonic forces involving high temperatures and directed pressures.

items: Metamorphic Progression Grade: Slate (low grade) → Phyllite → Schist → Gneiss (high grade) is frequently tested in Geography optional and GS papers.
Hornfels is uniquely identified with thermal/contact metamorphism and lacks directional foliation.
Mylonites and Fault Breccia serve as diagnostic rocks for dynamic metamorphism occurring along active fault zones.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Contact (Thermal) metamorphism occurs locally near igneous intrusions due to extreme heat, forming non-foliated rocks such as hornfels and marble.
Regional metamorphism spans widespread areas along convergent plate boundaries, driven by mountain-building forces, heat, and differential pressure.
Dynamic (Cataclastic) metamorphism takes place along fault lines under intense shear stress, producing crushed mineral textures such as mylonite.
Hydrothermal metamorphism is caused by hot, ion-rich fluids circulating through rock fractures, resulting in mineral re-crystallization.
